title: Finite distinguished extension tower for a constructible module
statement:
Fix a prime $\ell$, a finite intermediate field $E$ of $\overline{\mathbf Q}_\ell$
[def-weil-finite-subextension-directed-set], and a scheme $T$. Use the coefficient sheaves,
internal module categories $\mathcal M_T^c(E)$ and their ordinary derived categories of
[def-weil-pbc-condensed-e-module-category]. A module is locally finitely presented if it
admits a pro-etale covering on which it is a cokernel of a map between finite free modules.
A module is constructible if it has a finite locally closed stratification with constructible
underlying strata on each of which its inverse image is locally finitely presented.

Suppose the underlying space of $T$ is noetherian. Let $P$ be the property of being a piece
[def-weil-pbc-condensed-constructible-piece]. Put $P^{*0}=P$ and define recursively
$P^{*(r+1)}(B)$ to mean that there is a distinguished triangle $A\to B\to C\to A[1]$
[def-weil-triangulated-category] with $P(A)$ and $P^{*r}(C)$. For every constructible
$M\in\mathcal M_T^c(E)$ there exists $r\in\mathbf N$ with $P^{*r}(M[0])$.

proof.text: Induct on closed subsets $C$ of the original noetherian $T$, simultaneously for all closed immersions $Z\to T$ with image in $C$ and all constructible sheaves on $Z$. Closed subspaces remain noetherian and their strict-inclusion order is well founded.

Apply the one-step decomposition on $Z$. A piece gives $r=0$. Otherwise the image of the proper closed subscheme $Z^\prime$ in $T$ is strictly smaller than $C$: choose a point of $Z$ outside $Z^\prime$ and use injectivity of $Z\to T$. The induction hypothesis supplies a finite tower for the constructible sheaf on $Z^\prime$.

proof.text: Exact closed pushforward maps distinguished triangles and commutes with the single functor. A pushed piece is a piece: compose its closed immersion with the new closed immersion, using the canonical ordinary pushforward composition isomorphism. Induction on the finite tower therefore pushes it to $Z$ without changing its length. Prepend the one-step triangle to add one extension.
